mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without any additional conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3.0% signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which drives corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between the joint movement of HOUST and RSAFS and SPX 20-day returns is not significant (p>0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), labor market tightness leads to higher wage growth and corporate profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE is below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days without any additional conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI increase exceeding 3.0% signals accelerating inflation, which triggers central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and CPI inflation above 3.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening in response to high inflation, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% does not produce negative SPX 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 growth rate above 2.5% annually), supply chain pressures and capacity constraints lead to higher corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 annual growth exceeds 2.5%.
